es: Redactar una anécdota con escena de fondo, un hecho que la rompe, una intención interrumpida (was about to, was going to), un giro y un desenlace anticipado con would.

vocabulary.es: yo no tenía ni idea de que

teaching.en: The café was nearly empty, and the rain was tapping on the windows as I stirred a coffee that had long gone cold.
teaching.es: La cafetería estaba casi vacía, y la lluvia golpeteaba las ventanas mientras yo removía un café que ya se había enfriado.
teaching.explanationEs: Past continuous para el fondo de la escena: was tapping, con detalles que el lector percibe.

teaching.en: Suddenly, a woman sat down at my table, and I noticed that my wallet was no longer on the counter.
teaching.es: De repente, una mujer se sentó a mi mesa, y noté que mi cartera ya no estaba en el mostrador.
teaching.explanationEs: Suddenly + past simple: el hecho que rompe la escena.

noticed that my wallet was no longer on the counter.

teaching.explanationEs: Was about to + verbo base: estaba a punto de; se interrumpe con un hecho en past simple.

that my wallet was gone, and my face went hot.

teaching.en: I was going to call the police, but then the woman smiled and handed back my wallet, still warm from her pocket.

teaching.explanationEs: Was going to + verbo: intención en el pasado que no se cumple; but then introduce el giro.
segments: I was going to call the police, but then the woman
smiled and handed back my wallet, still warm from her pocket.

teaching.en: Little did I know that the stranger returning my wallet would become my business partner within a year.
teaching.es: Yo no tenía ni idea de que la desconocida que me devolvía la cartera se convertiría en mi socia en menos de un año.
teaching.explanationEs: Little al inicio pide inversión (did I know) y would anticipa el desenlace.

teaching.en: As luck would have it, the wallet had not been stolen; by a twist of fate, it had fallen into kind hands, to my relief.
teaching.es: Quiso la suerte que la cartera no hubiera sido robada; por un capricho del destino, había caído en buenas manos, para mi alivio.
teaching.explanationEs: El giro cambia lo que el lector creía; had been / had fallen sitúan lo ocurrido antes.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase presenta bien una escena de fondo y el hecho que la rompe?

choices.text: The café had been nearly empty when a woman was sitting down at my table.
The café was nearly empty when a woman sat down at my table.
The café was nearly empty when a woman sits down at my table.
The café nearly emptied when a woman was sat down at my table.

feedback.es: La escena de fondo va en past continuous (was nearly empty, aquí como estado) y el hecho que la rompe en past simple (sat down). Las demás mezclan tiempos sin motivo.

hint.es: Fondo en pasado; hecho que interrumpe en past simple.

origin.text: Sara is drafting the opening of her anecdote. She wants a background scene in the past continuous, followed by a sudden event in the past simple, without mixing the tenses.

prompt.es: Completa: «Iba a llamar a la policía al llegar a casa, pero ella me devolvió la cartera.»

feedback.es: Was going to + verbo base expresa una intención del pasado que no se cumple; as soon as I got home descarta was about to, que exige un momento inmediato.

hint.es: Intención pasada: was ___ to + verbo base.

origin.text: I was ___ to call the police as soon as I got home, but then the woman smiled and handed back my wallet, still warm from her pocket.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Yo no tenía ni idea de que se convertiría en mi socia.»

answer.text: Little did I know that she would become my partner

feedback.es: Little al inicio exige inversión (did I know) y would anticipa el desenlace desde el pasado.

hint.es: Little va primero, seguido del auxiliar did y el sujeto.

feedback.es: Cada frase ocupa un lugar distinto de la anécdota: fondo, hecho, giro y desenlace.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cuál es el giro de esta anécdota.

choices.text: The stranger turns out to be an old friend of the narrator.
The narrator misses the train after all and cancels the interview.
The kind stranger turns out to be linked to the narrator's interview.
The ticket turns out to be for a train going the wrong way.

feedback.es: El giro llega con «Little did I know»: el desconocido trabaja en la empresa de la entrevista y estará en el tribunal. Nada indica que fuera amigo ni que perdiera el tren.

origin.audio: I was standing in the queue at the station café, tapping my foot, when I realised that my train was about to leave. I was going to run for it, but the man in front of me turned to face me and handed me his ticket. “I'm not going anywhere,” he said. Little did I know that he worked at the company where I had an interview the next day and, as luck would have it, he would be one of the people asking the questions.

prompt.es: Completa: «Yo no tenía ni idea de que el hombre del banco me cambiaría la vida.»

feedback.es: Little did I know es la fórmula fija que anuncia un giro; al inicio exige inversión con did.

origin.text: It was a perfectly ordinary Tuesday. ___ did I know that the quiet man on the bench would change my life.

prompt.es: Escribe una anécdota de unas 150 palabras con escena, giro y desenlace.

answer.text: It was a grey afternoon, and the rain was tapping on the windows of the library. I was about to return a book when I noticed a small note between the pages. Suddenly, my curiosity woke up. It was a phone number, and below it someone had written: “Call me if you find this.” I was going to throw the note away, but then I remembered how quiet the library could feel on a wet day, so I phoned. A woman answered at once. “Finally,” she said, laughing. “I left it there three years ago, as a joke.” We talked for an hour. Little did I know that she would become my business partner, and that we would open a small shop together. To my relief, the shop was an immediate success, and the note is still on the wall.
accepted: It was a grey afternoon, and the rain was tapping on the windows of the library. I was about to return a book when I noticed a small note between the pages. Suddenly, my curiosity woke up. It was a phone number, and below it someone had written: “Call me if you find this.” I was going to throw the note away, but then I remembered how quiet the library could feel on a wet day, so I phoned. A woman answered at once. “Finally,” she said, laughing. “I left it there three years ago, as a joke.” We talked for an hour. Little did I know that she would become my business partner, and that we would open a small shop together. To my relief, the shop was an immediate success, and the note is still on the wall.

It was a rainy evening, and the wind was blowing hard outside the station. A few people were waiting quietly in the dark. I was about to get on the last bus when it dawned on me that my wallet was not in my bag. My heart was beating very fast. I was going to ask the driver for help, but a young woman handed me a ticket. “Don't worry,” she said. “Buy me a coffee one day.” I thanked her and sat by the window. Little did I know that I would meet her again. Two weeks later, she came into my new office, and she would become my best friend for the rest of my life, and my business partner too.

feedback.es: Una buena anécdota abre con una escena en pasado continuo, la rompe con un hecho, usa was about to / was going to y anticipa el final con would (Little did I know…).

origin.text: Situación: una tarde de lluvia en la biblioteca de tu barrio. Ibas a devolver un libro cuando viste una nota con un número de teléfono entre las páginas. Ibas a tirarla, pero llamaste. Giro: la persona que contestó resultó ser tu futura socia. Escribe la anécdota en primera persona, de unas 150 palabras, con: escena de fondo, hecho que la rompe, was about to, was going to y un desenlace con Little did I know y would.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere el narrador sobre el resultado de la entrevista.

choices.text: That Mr Hall gave the narrator the job only as a favour, despite a weak interview.
That the interview had been arranged in advance by Mr Hall.
That the narrator had known who Mr Hall was all along.
That a small act of kindness helped the narrator get the job.

feedback.es: El narrador no lo dice, pero «he remembered my face» y el contrato un mes después sugieren que el gesto amable ayudó; el texto no habla de un favor ni de una entrevista amañada.

origin.audio: It was a wet Sunday, and the train to Bristol was packed. I was sitting by the window, tapping my foot on the floor, when a man across from me dropped his wallet. I was about to call out when I noticed a card sticking out of it: “If lost, please return to Mr Hall.” I handed it back and thought nothing more of it. Little did I know that Mr Hall owned the company where I had applied for a job. As luck would have it, he remembered my face on the day of the interview, and within a month I had signed my contract.

prompt.es: Completa: «Iba a salir cuando caí en la cuenta de que no había enviado el contrato.»

feedback.es: It dawned on me es la expresión fija para darse cuenta de algo de golpe; no admite otro verbo en esta construcción.

origin.text: I was about to leave the office when it ___ on me that I had never sent the contract, and the client was waiting for it.

prompt.es: ¿Qué efecto busca el narrador con el arranque de este texto?

choices.text: To build tension by contrasting a calm scene with what follows.
To prepare the reader for a funny, light-hearted anecdote.
To show that the narrator is bored by an ordinary life.
To explain how the narrator came to be on a ferry.

feedback.es: La escena tranquila (martes, lluvia, café) contrasta con el desenlace anunciado con would: así se crea expectación sin revelar el giro. No es una anécdota cómica ni explica el viaje.

origin.text: It was an ordinary Tuesday. The rain was tapping on the windows, and I was halfway through my second coffee, thinking about nothing more serious than dinner. Nothing, absolutely nothing, suggested that by six o'clock I would be standing on a ferry with a stranger's suitcase in my hands.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Caí en la cuenta de que mi paraguas seguía en el tren.»

answer.text: It dawned on me that my umbrella was still on the train

feedback.es: It dawned on me introduce el descubrimiento; después, that + la cláusula con el hecho en pasado (was still on the train).

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la frase final de la narradora?

choices.text: That the two guests had not heard anything about the wedding.
That the others knew about the speech and avoided the subject.
That the narrator wanted the guests to mention the speech.
That her brother had asked her to keep the secret.

feedback.es: Que les hubieran pedido callar implica que conocían el asunto: su silencio no era ignorancia, sino discreción. El alivio de la narradora era prematuro.

origin.text: We had booked the house months in advance, and we were looking forward to a quiet week. As luck would have it, the only other guests were two people from our own street, and, to my relief, nobody mentioned my brother's wedding speech. Little did I know that they had been told to keep quiet about it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Para mi alivio, el autobús también iba tarde, así que no había perdido nada.»

feedback.es: To my relief es la expresión fija para indicar que algo salió mejor de lo temido; no admite otra palabra.

origin.text: I ran all the way to the stop, sure that I had missed the last bus. To my ___, the bus was late too, so I had not missed anything after all.
